newsitem.title: USA: USDA unveils PL480 country allocations for FY97.
newsitem.headline: USDA unveils PL480 country allocations for FY97.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Monday unveiled its preliminary Public Law 480 (PL 480) allocations for fiscal year 1997, making available $205 million for 21 countries to cover commodity financing.

Under PL 480, USDA provides low cost loans to developing countries to buy U.S. farm goods. For fiscal year 1997, the program has $226.9 million for financing and $13.9 million for ocean freight costs. USDA said it would make additional allocations or change existing ones as the year progresses.

Among the larger allocations, USDA said it allocated $21 million to Jordan to buy wheat and rice; $20 million to Georgia to buy wheat plus $2 million for ocean freight and $15 million to Armenia to buy wheat plus $1.5 million for freight.
USDA also said it allocated $10 million to Angola, El Salvador, Lithuania, Moldova, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Ukraine.
Mary Chambliss, USDA deputy administrator for export credits said top commodity sold under the food aid program was wheat or wheat flour.

"By far the major commodity we provide under food aid programs is wheat," she said in an interview on USDA Radio. "It usually runs 80, 90 percent of the total program because its the basic food commodity in these countries."
